subject: Security exhibit: evidence owners, pen-test timing, and redline package
messages:
From: Sara Parker <sara.parker@atlashealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Miles Chen <miles.chen@atlashealth.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit clarifications & pen-test guardrails

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for sending the draft order form last night. A few quick asks from Atlas InfoSec/legal so we can move the MSA + Order Form forward:

- Can you confirm the expected evidence cadence for SOC 2 artifacts (annual report vs. continuous evidence uploads)? We want to understand how Redwood will make the attestation and supporting artifacts available.
- Pen-test wording: we need clarity around timing (notice window), whether access is ephemeral/staging only, and what logs (retention/format) Redwood will provide.
- Ownership: who will own the upload of evidence artifacts (SOC report, pen-test report excerpts, control mapping)? Atlas prefers a single contact.

If you can share a short evidence matrix or sample artifacts that would help internal reviewers. We also may need to loop in procurement if there are changes to inspection rights.

Thanks — happy to set a 30-min call next week if that’s easier.

Sara Parker
Head of Information Security
Atlas Health

Attachments: none
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Parker <sara.parker@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 09:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit clarifications & pen-test guardrails

Sara — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers and next steps below; attaching a redline package and an evidence matrix for your review.

High-level answers:
- SOC 2: Redwood provides an annual SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) plus an evidence matrix that maps control areas to artifact owners. For customers that need higher cadence we can provide scoped artifact uploads and access to logs via a shared drive (see attached matrix).
- Pen-test: we propose a 30-day rolling notice window for customer-run pen tests with access scoped to a staging environment. Redwood will provide authentication logs and request/response sampling for the agreed window; log retention for evidence is 90 days by default, extendable under Dedicated/Private contracts.
- Evidence ownership: Redwood will nominate a single evidence owner for Atlas — Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.com) — who will coordinate uploads and handoffs with your team.

What I’ve attached: Atlas_Security_Exhibit_v3_redlines.pdf (redline of security exhibit + suggested language), evidence_matrix_atlas_v1.xlsx (owner mapping + sample artifacts).

Next steps / asks:
1) Karthik — can your team review the redlines and confirm whether the pen-test notice window and retention language are acceptable to Legal? If not, propose specific alternate language.
2) Atlas — if you can review the matrix and confirm the preferred evidence owner on your side we’ll lock that into the order form.
3) If both sides agree we’ll schedule a 30-min sync to finalize.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Atlas_Security_Exhibit_v3_redlines.pdf (pdf, 78 KB)
- evidence_matrix_atlas_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 24 KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit clarifications & pen-test guardrails

Evelyn / team — reviewed the redline package this morning. High-level legal notes below (I’ve attached a tiny snippet with proposed wording):

- Inspection phrasing: the current draft uses broad "inspection rights" language. We should narrow to "bounded inspection" (staging-only, scoped controls, and timeboxed windows) and reference a specific evidence matrix. That reduces procurement pushback.
- Pen-test notice: propose a 30-day notice with the ability for Redwood to request a 7-day deferral for operational risk (e.g., active incidents). We should explicitly exclude production access unless mutually agreed in writing.
- Logs & retention: accept 90-day baseline retention; if Atlas requires longer retention, add a commercial footnote (Dedicated/Private only).
- Redaction & confidentiality: pen-test reports will be shared in redacted form (sensitive exploit details redacted) with an NDA clause referenced in the exhibit.

Attachments:
- legal_redline_snippet.txt (txt, 2 KB) — includes the specific replacement language for the inspection/pen-test clauses.

Ben — please confirm you’re happy to be the evidence owner and operational contact for uploads. Marissa — can you add a short ops runbook (1-pager) to the Drive folder so Atlas can see the handoff process?

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround and the materials. A couple of clarifications from Atlas legal before we lock: 

- Pen-test timing: we’d prefer a target window in early September rather than a later rolling window. Is Redwood able to support a customer-initiated test during the week of Sept 6 (staging only)?
- Evidence uploads: Atlas will designate an internal evidence coordinator (Sara will confirm name tomorrow). Please confirm Ben will have upload access and we’ll get a short ops runbook (Marissa).
- SOC 2: can Redwood confirm the SOC 2 Type II report will be provided as a signed PDF to be uploaded to our secure folder? Also confirm the scope (in-scope systems/components) — if you can include a one-paragraph scope summary in the Drive link that would speed review.

If those items are acceptable we can set a 30-min signoff call on Wed or Thu next week.

Miles Chen
Counsel, Contracts & Procurement
Atlas Health
